Subject: Staged cutover & surge action plan (MAP embedded) — next 30 days

Hi Tom / Emily —

Thanks again for the signature — excited to get LatticeHealth onto Redwood Dedicated. Attached is the working MAP that embeds the post-signature implementation plan (rollout, canary, migration, training) alongside acceptance gates. I tried to keep the first 30 days prescriptive so your PMs and ours can align on the runbook.

High level calls-to-action in this version:
- Week 1 (Provisioning): Reserved cluster allocation + initial test model image; redwood infra will hand over access details.
- Week 2 (Canary): Small-batch traffic routing to canary pool (50 qps), run the canary checklist and smoke tests.
- Weeks 3–4 (Migration & Training): Gradual traffic shift in 10% increments, two instructor-led training sessions for ops and SRE.

Please review tabs: "Milestones", "Canary Checklist", "Training Roster", and "Rollback Triggers". I also attached our canary checklist PDF for quick reference.

Questions for you before we lock dates:
1) Are there blackout dates for your infra team in the next 4 weeks?
2) Preferred days/times for the two training sessions (we suggest Tue/Thu mornings PST).
3) Any additional compliance evidence we should add to the MAP before we share with your SOC team?

Next steps: If that looks good, Marissa and Jonas will propose concrete slots and I'll send a one-page mutual action summary to your procurement contact.

Best,
Hannah

Hannah — thanks for the clear plan and the MAP. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifications: 

- Blackout: our clinical ops have a freeze from 3/18–3/20 (regional maintenance). Avoid major shifts then.
- Training: Tue/Thu mornings PST works for most folks; prefer 10:00–11:30 PT.
- Compliance: We'll need an explicit list of what audit logs are retained and for how long (HIPAA scope). Can you add an evidence column in the MAP that points to the logs/locations?

Two small asks re canary: 
1) Can we run canary traffic with a synthetic test suite that includes PII-scrubbed payloads?
2) If the canary fails one key latency gate but passes correctness checks, what is Redwood's default fallback?

I'll loop in PS if we need scheduling.

—Tom

Head of Platform, LatticeHealth

Tom — great questions. Answering inline and proposing updates we will make today: 

- Blackout noted (3/18–3/20) — we'll mark those as "no-change windows" in the Milestones tab.
- Training slot confirmed: we'll propose Tue 3/22 10:00–11:30 PT and Thu 3/24 10:00–11:30 PT as first options.
- Audit logs: we will add an "Evidence" column pointing to the log retention policy and sample S3 paths (redwood-managed for Hosted; for Dedicated we provide the retention configuration and KMS key id). I'll attach a short PDF with the retention matrix (HIPAA scope: access logs, API call traces, admin actions).

Canary specifics: 
1) Synthetic tests — yes, please use PII-scrubbed payloads. We'll provide a test harness and a script that scrubs payloads locally before sending.
2) Fallback behavior — default is an automatic rollback to the previous stable model variant + an immediate notification to both teams. If latency is borderline (within 10% of threshold) we will hold and open a joint incident call; if it exceeds threshold we will roll back automatically. We'll add those rules under "Rollback Triggers".

I'll update the MAP and share a new workbook by EOD. Jonas — can you draft the short evidence PDF and the snippet for the test-harness README?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
